learning_outcomes.text: Acquire theoretical knowledge concerning thermodynamics, machines, acoustics, and lighting technology.
Acquire practical skills in evaluating the main environmental phenomena of heat transmission, acoustic waves, and light waves in living environments.
Provide students with theoretical knowledge and practical skills for the analysis of these phenomena and the recognition of their effects on human health.
Understand the theory of thermodynamics and heat transmission.
Understand the theory of thermal machines and thermodynamic cycles.
Understand the theory and technique of air conditioning.
Understand the theory and phenomenology of indoor and outdoor microclimate in buildings.
Understand acoustic analysis and lighting technology techniques in indoor and outdoor building environments.
Evaluate the principles of thermodynamics and their applied consequences.
Analyze thermal machines and their thermodynamic cycles.
Analyze the main mechanisms of heat exchange.
Evaluate the quality of indoor environments and their microclimatic characteristics.
Evaluate the characteristics and main acoustic and lighting parameters and their effect on human health.

syllabus_topics: Applied Thermodynamics: Thermodynamic quantities, closed and open thermodynamic systems, state quantities, phase rule, Clapeyron P-v diagram, principles of thermodynamics, zero principle and temperature concept (thermal equilibrium), first principle and energy conservation, machines, efficiencies, second principle and energy quality, entropy, T-s entropy diagram, enthalpy, exergy, thermal machines and their energetic and exergetic efficiency, mechanical components and technology, construction of thermodynamic transformations on T-S and P-v graphs.
Otto, Diesel, Brayton, Rankine, Rankine-Hirn, Inverse Rankine Cycles.

Air Conditioning: Psychrometric quantities (specific humidity, relative humidity, dew point temperature, wet bulb temperature), psychrometer, psychrometric diagram, air treatments (summer and winter treatment of humid air in an all-air system), description of an air conditioning system.

Heat Transmission: Modes of heat transmission (conduction, convection, radiation, adduction), thermal insulating materials, applied examples in civil engineering (monolayer, multilayer walls, with and without internal heat generation, glazed walls), applied examples in industrial engineering (insulation of pipes, heat exchangers, cooling fins).

Lighting Technology: Visual well-being, photometric quantities, lighting design objectives, overview of street lighting, lighting design of enclosed spaces (total flux method, point-to-point method), natural lighting (average daylight factor), luxmeter and luminance meter.

Acoustics: Acoustic quantities and their levels, acoustic spectra, frequency bands (octaves and one-third octaves), sound propagation, reverberation, absorption, reflection and transmission for acoustic energy, sound absorption (porous sound-absorbing panels, perforated resonant absorbing panels, vibrating panels), sound insulation (sound insulation power and mass law), sound and noise, qualitative aspects of auditory sensation, noise disturbance evaluation indices, A-weighted sound pressure level LpA(t), normal audiogram, A-weighting curve, A-weighted equivalent continuous sound level LAeq,T, psychoacoustics (effects of noise on humans, shift of hearing threshold), sound level meter, legislation and technical standards.
assessment_rules: The exam will consist of 4 written questions, of which 2 will be general and 2 specific. A final oral exam will follow.
